issues.legal_issue: Review jurisdiction under Order XLVII Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure is limited to the prescribed grounds and cannot be used to rehear evidence, reassess the merits, or function as an appeal.
New evidence arising after the decree cannot ordinarily support review, and review evidence must be relevant, important, of unimpeachable quality, and unavailable earlier despite due diligence.

A reserved-forest notification under the Andhra Pradesh Forest Act, 1967 changes the land’s legal character, extinguishes unclaimed rights, and cannot be collaterally challenged after the statutory proceedings become final.

A civil suit seeking declaration of title to land declared reserved forest is not maintainable when the statutory forest proceedings have not been specifically challenged and the necessary statutory authority has not been joined.
A revenue authority has no jurisdiction to alter or determine rights in land after proceedings declaring it reserved forest have concluded under the Andhra Pradesh Forest Act, 1967.
